### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **60** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 38651598a7d8e72151ddedde3eb02e4fb0c207b6`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **26** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 38651598a7d8e72151ddedde3eb02e4fb0c207b6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9a70c771c3905ce86de79963730204d7fb3fcb13` — the merge of head `eb7990be468b9b2c888d52098d7a07c6c766eb05` into base `38651598a7d8e72151ddedde3eb02e4fb0c207b6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9a70c771c3905ce86de79963730204d7fb3fcb13 && git checkout 9a70c771c3905ce86de79963730204d7fb3fcb13
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 38651598a7d8e72151ddedde3eb02e4fb0c207b6 eb7990be468b9b2c888d52098d7a07c6c766eb05 && git checkout -B drift-repro 38651598a7d8e72151ddedde3eb02e4fb0c207b6 && git merge --no-ff eb7990be468b9b2c888d52098d7a07c6c766eb05

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 38651598a7d8e72151ddedde3eb02e4fb0c207b6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 38651598a7d8e72151ddedde3eb02e4fb0c207b6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The PR's committed file list is four paths — `.changeset/27744-plugin-driver-conformance-kit.md`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin-driver-conformance.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin-driver-conformance.test.ts` — +1424/−0; no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed register row, no `(narrowing)` arm, so no schema, rules or narrowing face and no ④. Both were read; #27741 contributes nothing to this head beyond the wiring item answered in ③.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface widened on `@objectstack/objectql`'s root entry** (`exports["."]`, `dist/index.*`): six value exports — `createPluginDriverConformance`, `runPluginDriverConformance`, `definePluginDriverConformanceSuite`, `pluginDriverConformanceFixtures`, `PLUGIN_DRIVER_CONFORMANCE_FIXTURE_NAMES`, `PluginDriverConformanceFailure` — and fifteen types, all re-exported from the new module. The changeset's "New exports" list names exactly these. `Clause-②: yes` is the right declaration for it. **Right.**
2. **No accept set moves.** The `index.ts` hunk is additions only; no existing export is renamed, removed or re-typed. `external-driver-floor.ts`, `external-driver-errors.ts`, `driver-query-in-memory.ts` and `driver-connect-errors.ts` are read by the kit and not touched, so the engine's floor over a plugin driver behaves at this head exactly as on `main`. The changeset's "Nothing existing changes" holds. **Right.**
3. **The kit asserts the floor's actual contract**, read against the head tree's `external-driver-floor.ts` and `external-driver-errors.ts`: the floor sends the driver `where`, `orderBy` and `limit: EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP + 1`, never `offset` or `fields`, in ONE `inner.find` per read — so `flooredRead` reading `answers[0]` is the whole answer, `shapeCase`'s `{ limit: ROW_LIMIT }` is the plainest read the floor sends, and `floorOrderCase`'s per-page `mustInclude = all` is what the floor needs. A driver throw with a status in `EXTERNAL_READ_REFUSED_STATUSES` (400, 404, 422) reaches the caller as `ExternalReadRefusedError`; the kit's `judgeReadThrow` plus the `instanceof ExternalReadRefusedError` check match that door. Any other read throw is `DatasourceUnavailableError` (503, reason `remote`); the outage case's `instanceof DatasourceUnavailableError` matches. A write throw with a status in `EXTERNAL_WRITE_REFUSED_STATUSES` is `ExternalWriteRefusedError` with `code === EXTERNAL_WRITE_REFUSED_CODE` and status 422; `writeCase` matches. The PR body's "refuse with 400, 404 or 422" and "422 EXTERNAL_WRITE_REFUSED" / "503 ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE" are the floor's own numbers. **Right.**
4. **The oracle is the spec's published tables**, imported through the `@objectstack/spec/data` barrel (`export *` of `filter-logic-conformance`, `filter-text-conformance`, `temporal-conformance`, `pagination-conformance` and `filter-lowering`). The fixture field maps match the row shapes: `filter_logic` a/b/c/d/owner/status/parent_object/parent_id, `filter_text` name/score, `pagination` status/rank/name, `temporal` at (`datetime`) / on (`date`) — the temporal cases filter only `at` (33 leaves) and `on` (9), so `isDatetimeColumn: column === 'at'` is the correct declared-type reader and dropping `writerForm` / `why` from `TEMPORAL_ROWS` drops spec-authoring metadata, not columns. **Right.**
5. **Declared non-coverage is real and named in both places** (PR body and module comment): `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` rows with `expectRejection: true` are refused by the engine's door before a driver is asked, so they test the engine; `TEMPORAL_TIME_CASES` has no comparand class in the floor yet. Skipping them is a truthful gap, not a silent one. **Right.**
6. **Pushdown measured, not declared.** `DriverCapabilitiesSchema`'s TSDoc on `main` and the semantic migration entry `17.driver-capabilities-inert-bits-removed` confirm the query bits are gone, so the card's "`supports`-declared pushdown" premise could not be implemented as written; the kit's per-case `exact | superset | refused` plus `order: honoured | not-honoured` is the only honest reading and is what the P3 credential can key on. The premise correction is right.
7. **No new dependency edge.** `resolveFilterTokens` comes from `@objectstack/core`, already a runtime dependency of `@objectstack/objectql` and already imported by ten non-test modules reachable from `index.ts`; `@objectstack/core` does not depend on `@objectstack/objectql`. No cycle, nothing added to `package.json`. **Right.**
8. **`introspectSchema` shape** is judged against `IntrospectedSchema` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/schema-diff-service.ts`: `dialect` string, `introspectedAt` ISO 8601, `tables` record, column `name` / `type` / `nullable` / `primaryKey`, `indexes` optional with absence meaningful — the kit checks indexes only when the key is present, which is the contract's own rule. **Right.**
9. **Runtime strings carry no tracker number.** Every `PluginDriverConformanceFailure` message a vendor author reads names the query, the rule and the fix; the only `#NNNN` tokens in the new file are in comments. The `// [#27744]` in `index.ts` is a code comment in the file's existing convention. **Right.**
10. **Floor memoisation is used correctly.** `floored()` wraps a fresh recording Proxy per read so `createExternalDriverFloor`'s per-driver WeakMap never hands back a stale floor; `writeCase` floors the raw driver of a fresh `open()` per probe. **Right.**
11. **Test file**: batteries pinned by count against the spec tables per tier, unique case ids, lazy setup, unknown tier refused, four passing driver shapes, eleven mutants each pinned to the case id that names the broken rule, teardown-once, and the suite form registered under vitest's own `describe` / `it` / `afterAll`. Test Core (8 shards) is green on the head. **Right.**
12. Observation, not a finding: `floorOrderCase` labels every order case `pushdown: 'exact'` because the floor sends it no `where`; the measurement that case carries is `order`. Harmless, and the report shape is documented.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27744-plugin-driver-conformance-kit.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`, body carrying `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, both line-initial; the PR body carries the same two lines. **Consistent with the diff**: the diff publishes new exports from a released package (so not `skip-changeset`), adds no authorable key, value or type (so the kind is `none`).
- Level rule (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` level axis, maintainer ruling A of 2026-10-21): the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone — `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. So `patch` beside `Clause-②: yes` / `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right level. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on the head, the gate's own reading of the same lines. `@objectstack/objectql` sits in the `fixed` group, so the lockstep bump is `patch` for the group — consistent.
- `Clause-②:` line: `yes`, no arm — right for a widening of the public surface with no narrowing. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed (kind `none`, no `(narrowing)` arm). No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition owed. Dogfood battery n/a (no `!` in the title, no narrowing arm) — right.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`open_questions[0]`** (os-dev-report 6511097820): close #27744 with this PR, or keep `Part of` until driver-odata runs the kit. **Answered by the PM ruling** in PR comment 6511123974: this PR closes #27744 (`Fixes`); the driver-odata wiring goes to whichever of #27741 (PR #27796) / this PR lands second; the guide pointer goes to #27747. At this head the PR body still reads `Part of #27744`; under the option the ruling picked, the body edit is the owning seat's act (the dev's option A names the PM as the editor), the `PR-body guards` check is `success` on the current body, and a body edit moves no byte of the reviewed tree, so this record stands across it. **Owning seat: edit the body to `Fixes #27744` before landing.** Not a must-fix.
2. **Acceptance note — premise correction** (`supports`-declared pushdown does not exist): answered right, ① item 6.
3. **Acceptance note — not covered, deliberately** (text rejection rows, `TEMPORAL_TIME_CASES`): accepted, ① item 5; a vendor reads the gap in the module comment.
4. **Acceptance note — no new package**: the card allowed `@objectstack/objectql` or a small test-kit package; placing the kit beside `createExternalDriverFloor` so a vendor tests against the floor of the version it installs is the better reading, and it stays inside the claim's file surface (`packages/objectql/src/**`). Accepted.
5. **`out_of_scope_findings`** (two, carriers named, not filed): the driver-odata wiring (carrier #27741) and the guide pointer in `content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx` (carrier #27747) — both placed by the PM ruling above. Answered.
6. **Card task item 2** ("driver-odata runs it in this repository as the first consumer") is not in this diff by the card's own serial constraint ("do not edit its package. Wire it in a later PR, or say in the report how the two meet"); the report says how they meet. Answered by the ruling.

Zero failures. The docs-drift comment is advisory and names no hand-written page this diff falsifies (the kit is new; the guide pointer is #27747's).
9. **Escalation — the brief's card number.** The dispatch brief named card #27741 for a PR whose body, claim and handoff name #27744. Read both; judged against #27744. The seat that writes the next brief for this lane should carry the PR's own card.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `eb7990be468b9b2c888d52098d7a07c6c766eb05`
Local-runs: none

Delta review on record 6511619545 (head `07def8ccc7c559ac98a6b10b2201012de97d2f70`, PASS, declaration face), by the same reviewer. Face unchanged: the `Clause-②: yes` declaration alone (PR body and changeset, both line-initial); no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed register row (`packages/drivers/**` is not one), no `(narrowing)` arm, so no schema, rules or narrowing face and no ④. Inputs: card #27744 (body, claim 6510468826, os-dev-report 6511097820, claim amendment 6512765336), PR #27798 body, file list and net diff against `main` at the head (five paths, +1488/−0), the 48 check-runs on the head, and the PR comments (docs-drift 6511094573 as re-run on this head, handoff 6511123974, claims 6511469408 and 6513131440, record 6511619545).

**What moved since the previous record** — two commits. (a) `beacfa67` merges `origin/main` at `0a4b0fb2` (38 commits, #27796 driver-odata among them) into the branch: the PR's four paths are byte-identical on both sides of the merge (a diff of `07def8cc..beacfa67` restricted to them is empty), and the merge's diff against `0a4b0fb2` is exactly those four paths at +1424/−0, so the merge carries nothing of the PR's own and nothing of `main`'s is re-judged here — it is `main`. In the kit's dependency closure `main` moved `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (8 lines), `secret-fields.ts` (4) and `external-driver-floor.test.ts` (a test); `external-driver-floor.ts` and `external-driver-errors.ts`, the contract the kit asserts, did not move, and the spec tables the kit reads did not move. (b) `eb7990be` adds one file, `packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/odata-driver.conformance-kit.test.ts` (+64), which runs the exported kit over the OData driver and the in-process OData v4 service that #27796 landed. Sections the move does not touch stand as judged in record 6511619545, named below.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface of `@objectstack/objectql`**: the `index.ts` hunk (six value exports, fifteen types), `plugin-driver-conformance.ts` and `plugin-driver-conformance.test.ts` are byte-identical to the head record 6511619545 judged. Items 1–12 of that record's ① stand as judged, including the premise correction (pushdown measured, not declared) and the declared non-coverage.
2. **No new public surface, no accept-set move.** The new file is a `*.test.ts` under `packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/`; `@objectstack/driver-odata` ships `files: ["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md"]` and its `exports` point at `dist/index.*`, so the package's published surface is what `main` publishes. No source module of either package changes. **Right.**
3. **The new test calls the kit as the kit is exported.** `definePluginDriverConformanceSuite({ describe, it, afterAll }, options, title)` — the api object matches `PluginDriverConformanceTestApi` (`describe`, `it`, optional `afterAll`), the third positional `title` exists with that meaning, and `setup` may answer a `PluginDriverConformanceTarget` synchronously (`Target | Promise of Target`); `{ driver }` with `object` absent defaults to `fixture.object`, which `registerExternalObject({ name: fixture.object, external: { remoteName: 'Rows' } })` binds to the service's one entity set. `tiers` absent ⇒ `['floor']`; the header's reason for leaving the `direct` tier out is the driver's own design (`count` refuses a `where` it cannot translate whole; `$filter` is a superset by rule), so the opt-in tier would fail by design, not by defect. **Right.**
4. **The EDM map is total over the kit's field types.** `Record of PluginDriverConformanceFixture['fields'][string]['type'] to EdmType` — the kit's `PluginDriverConformanceField.type` is exactly `text | number | datetime | date`, and the map names all four; a fifth type added to the kit later fails `tsc` here, which is the "fails in this repository first" the header promises. Read against the service's `comparable`: `Edm.Double` compares as a number, `Edm.DateTimeOffset` through `Date.parse`, `Edm.Date` lexically on ISO text — each consistent with the spec rows and with the kit's shape case (a number stays a number; an instant comes back as the stored string). **Right.**
5. **The key is right for the floor's row contract.** The first `ServiceProperty` is `id` (`Edm.String`, `nullable: false`), which the service's `$metadata` declares as the key; the kit's fixture rows carry a string `id` on every row. In the driver's `bind`, the property named `id` maps to field `id`, so `idIsKeyAlias` is false, `toRemote` sends `id` on a create, and `idOf` answers the key's text — string ids, no `_id`, which `judgeRows` requires. **Right.**
6. **Paging is exercised, not assumed.** `serverPageSize: 5` makes every floor read (`limit: EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP + 1`, so `$top` is set) span several server pages; the driver follows `@odata.nextLink` through `followLink` (same origin as `CONFORMANCE_ROOT`) until `limit` rows or no link. **Right.**
7. **Both collations are the kit's intended use.** Under the `case-insensitive` service the driver's `eq` / `contains` on text widen, the floor narrows, and the kit records `superset` while asserting the floored answer equals the table — the "never narrower" rule of `filter.ts` made checkable by a consumer that is not the driver's own test. **Right.**
8. **Outage probe reaches the right door.** `setupUnavailable` hands the driver a `fetch` that throws `TypeError`; the transport rethrows an `Error` with no `status` (`could not be reached`), the floor's `remoteFailure` answers `DatasourceUnavailableError` (503), and the first request of every verb is `$metadata`, so `find`, `findOne` and `count` all hit it. `outageCase` checks `instanceof DatasourceUnavailableError`. **Right.**
9. **Write probes are judged against the service's actual answers**, default fixture `filter_logic` (rows `1`–`4`): a create of `{ id: '1', a: 'x' }` posts `{ id: '1', a: 'x' }` (item 5), the service answers 409 (`An entity with this key already exists.`), 409 is in `EXTERNAL_WRITE_REFUSED_STATUSES` (400, 404, 409, 412, 422), the floor throws `ExternalWriteRefusedError` with `EXTERNAL_WRITE_REFUSED_CODE`, and `writeCase` passes `refused` — the inline comment names the mechanism that fires. The update `'1', { a: 'changed' }` patches `Rows('1')`, which exists, answers 200 with the entity, and passes `accepted`. The kit opens a fresh setup per probe, so the create's 409 and the update touch no shared read session. **Right.**
10. **Introspect probe.** The driver offers `introspectSchema()`, built from the service's own `$metadata` (`metadataFor`): `tables.Rows` with `name` / `type` / `nullable` / `primaryKey` per column, `dialect: 'odata-4.0'`, `introspectedAt` ISO, no `indexes` key — the kit checks indexes only when present. **Right.**
11. **Not a duplicate of `odata-driver.conformance.test.ts`** (#27796): that file runs the spec case-sets through the `ObjectQL` engine with the driver on an external datasource; this one runs the exported kit's own floor over the raw driver — the first in-repo consumer of the kit, which is the card's second task item. No test is deleted. **Right.**
12. **Gates the new file is subject to.** `@objectstack/objectql` is imported by package name, a `devDependency` (`workspace:*`) already on `main` with the vitest alias to `../../objectql/src/index.ts` (`check:test-source-alias` form); every relative import is same-package, so `check:cross-package-test-inputs` has nothing to see; the package's `tsconfig.json` includes `src/**/*`, so `tsc --noEmit` compiles the test (`TypeScript Type Check` green). No runtime string in the file carries a tracker number; the file carries none anywhere. The commit's trailers are the model-free pair. **Right.**
13. Observation, not a finding: `nullable` is unset on the non-key properties, which `metadataFor` writes as `Nullable="true"` — right for the fixtures (`d: null` rows), and immaterial to the kit, which reads nullability only through `introspectSchema()`'s shape.
